newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Owens Corning sees Asian revenue rise.
newsitem.headline: Owens Corning sees Asian revenue rise.

text.p: Owens Corning expects its revenues from Asia Pacific operations to rise fivefold to US$500 million by 2000, chairman Glen Hiner said on Wednesday.
"Growth rates in the Asia Pacific region are the fastest and we expect to see revenue reach US$500 million by the turn of the century," Hiner, also chief executive officer, told Reuters.
He said Asian sales now form a small percentage of overall company turnover, accounting for less than US$100 million, but it only started pursuing Asian business three years ago.
The company's overall turnover for 1996 was US$3.83 billion, six percent higher than the previous year.
Hiner said the company was on track to see total 1997 sales reach about US$4.1 billion, as forecast earlier.
Owens Corning, a manufacturer of composite and building materials, opened its regional office for Southeast Asia in Singapore on Wednesday.
The Singapore office will serve as a regional base for the sales of building materials and fibre glass reinforcements for composites in Southeast Asia, Hiner said.
He said this marked the company's commitment to expand its exports in the region and to provide marketing and technical support functions for customers and new business.
"The Singapore office will develop and implement a strategy within the ASEAN sector," he said.

Hiner said: "we've had a lot of concentration of our Asia Pacific business in China recently." In China, Owens Corning has manufacturing facilities in Changchun, Guangzhou, Shanghai, Nanjing and Anshan, and seven sales offices.
An application development center is being established in Shanghai, and there are plans for one in Southeast Asia.
"We also want to have a manufacturing presence and (location) will be determined by our people here," Hiner said.
The company is currently building a manufacturing plant in northern Bombay, India, and the aim is for 80 percent of output from that facility to be exported within Asia, Hiner said.
China's production, however, is consumed domestically, but one of its plants equipped with polystyrene foamboard technology, could potentially export product, Hiner said.

He said Owens Corning had not been as prompt in dealing with ASEAN opportunities in the past, but added that since starting its Asian Pacific headquarters in HongKong in 1994, bolder steps have been taken to achieve growth targets.
The aim is to have foreign business eventually account for about 30 to 35 percent of total revenue, he said.
Owens Corning is headquartered in Toledo, Ohio, and has about 19,000 employees worldwide, and manufacturing, sales and research facilities in more than 30 countries.
